name: gnu-chess
why: A classic GNU chess engine with a long history; charming and old-school, though a fairly familiar kind of program.

brief.what_it_is: GNU Chess is a chess-playing program from the GNU Project, currently at version 6.3.0. You can play against it in a terminal, but the homepage says it is more commonly used as a chess engine behind graphical frontends such as XBoard. The frontend or terminal supplies the moves and the engine returns its own. The homepage does not say what file formats it reads or writes beyond the opening book, which the Homebrew caveat describes as a PGN file.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as a free-software chess program in the GNU tradition, usable directly on a terminal or as an engine for graphical boards. It does not state a broader problem or idea beyond that.

commands_seen.context: Per the homepage, opens the GNU Chess documentation in the info reader.
Per the homepage, opens the GNU Chess manual page.
Per the homepage, prints a brief summary of options.

brief.install_notes: The homepage does not give install steps beyond pointing to the GNU FTP and mirrors. From the 6.3.x notes, gnuchess.ini is read from XDG_CONFIG_HOME or ~/.config/, and gnuchess.ini is generated from gnuchess.ini.in. The Homebrew caveat says the formula also downloads an opening book, a PGN file in the Cellar at share/doc/gnu-chess under the 6.3.0 directory, which can be added using gnuchess commands. No accounts or special hardware are mentioned.
brief.standout: It is a long-running GNU program that still targets the XBoard protocol world and is used more as an engine than as a standalone game. The ship-with-an-opening-book setup and the terminal-first plus engine-for-frontends split are old-school in a pleasant way.
brief.status: Appears maintained. The homepage names a current maintainer, Antonio Ceballos, describes the 6.3.x release changes, and shows a page update dated 2025/08/21. I did not check a release history or commit log, so the exact last release date is unknown.
brief.caveats: The homepage does not list platforms, build requirements, or the full command set. Its own release notes are brief. The Homebrew caveat says the opening book is a separate PGN download that has to be loaded by hand. The software is GPL-3.0 or later. The homepage does not discuss playing strength.
quotes: GNU Chess is a chess-playing program. It can be used to play chess against the computer on a terminal or, more commonly, as a chess engine for graphical chess frontends such as XBoard.
Development of GNU Chess, and GNU in general, is a volunteer effort, and you can contribute.
